extracted.intended_audience: issuers of securities registered under section 12, corporate management, corporate counsel, transfer agents, and accountants
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and content requirements for distributing written information statements to security holders (holders entitled to vote but from whom proxies are not solicited), including required items (Schedule 14C), filing and typographic rules, timing, and prohibitions against false or misleading statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — when information statement required
rubrics_metrics.description: In connection with every annual or other meeting of the holders of a class of securities registered pursuant to section 12 of the Act, the issuer shall transmit a written information statement to every security holder who is entitled to vote in regard to any matter to be acted upon at the meeting and from whom a proxy is not solicited on behalf of the management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to any annual or other meeting held on or after March 15, 1966. In the case of a class of securities in unregistered or bearer form, transmit only to those holders whose names and addresses are known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content parity with proxy material
rubrics_metrics.description: The information statement is required to contain substantially the same information as that which would be required in a proxy statement if proxies were solicited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For annual meetings the issuer is also required to transmit an annual report including financial statements comparable to those sent when proxies are solicited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report—financial statement content and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report accompanying or preceding the information statement shall contain such financial statements for the last fiscal year as will, in the opinion of management, adequately reflect the financial position and results of operations of the issuer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidated statements should be included if necessary to reflect adequately the issuer's position; differences in accounting principles that have a material effect must be noted and reconciled; financial statements shall be certified by independent public or certified public accountants unless (i) corresponding statements filed with the Commission are not required to be certified, or (ii) the Commission finds certification impracticable or unduly expensive. Management may condense details so long as omission does not make statements misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing preliminary copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Three preliminary copies of the information statement are required to be filed with the Commission at least ten days before the statement is sent to security holders, or such shorter period as the Commission may authorize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary copies must be clearly marked "Preliminary Copies"; filing is for Commission information and review, and printing of definitive copies should be deferred until staff comments are received and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing definitive copies and exchange filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Eight copies of the information statement in definitive form must be filed; three copies shall at the same time be filed with each national securities exchange upon which any security of the issuer is listed and registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitive copies shall be filed with, or mailed for filing to, the Commission not later than the date the statement is first sent or given to any security holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and typography requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The information included in the information statement shall be clearly presented and divided into groups according to subject matter and preceded by appropriate headings; where practicable and appropriate information should be presented in tabular form; all amounts shall be stated in figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All printed information statements shall be set in roman type at least as large as 10-point modern type except that financial statements and other statistical/tabular matter may be set in roman type at least as large as 8-point modern type; all type shall be leaded at least 2 points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for beneficial owners through record holders
rubrics_metrics.description: If the issuer knows that securities entitled to vote are held of record by a broker, dealer, bank, voting trustee, or their nominees, the issuer must inquire whether other persons are beneficial owners and must supply the record holder with enough copies of the information statement and annual report to enable the record holder to furnish copies to beneficial owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuer shall pay the reasonable expenses of the record holder in transmitting the material to beneficial owners; charges should not exceed out‑of‑pocket expenses including reasonable clerical expenses; follows reimbursement provisions of Rule 14a‑2(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for sending information statement to holders
rubrics_metrics.description: The information statement shall be sent or given at least 20 days prior to the meeting date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary filing schedule and any Commission-authorized shorter periods are separate; ensure distribution timetable complies with both sending and filing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: False or misleading statements prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No information statement shall contain any statement which, at the time and in the light of the circumstances under which it is made, is false or misleading with respect to any material fact, or which omits to state any material fact necessary to make the statements not false or misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing with or examination by the Commission does not mean the Commission has found the material accurate or approved its contents; issuers must not represent otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule 14C Item 1 — Adoption of Schedule 14A items
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnish the information called for by all of the items of Schedule 14A of Regulation 14A (17 CFR 240.14a‑101) (other than Items 1, 3, and 4 thereof) which would be applicable to any matter to be acted upon at the meeting if proxies were to be solicited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1 imports much of the Schedule 14A disclosure framework; respond only to applicable items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule 14C Item 2 — Statement that proxies are not solicited
rubrics_metrics.description: The following statement shall be set forth on the first page of the information statement in bold-face type: 'We Are Not Asking You For A Proxy and You Are Requested Not To Send Us A Proxy'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required exact wording and prominent placement (first page, bold-face).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule 14C Item 3 — Date, time and place of meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: State the date, time and place of the meeting of security holders, unless such information is otherwise disclosed in material furnished to security holders with the information statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these logistical details unless already provided elsewhere in distributed materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule 14C Item 4 — Interest of certain persons in or opposition to matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe briefly any substantial interest, direct or indirect, by security holdings or otherwise, of each of the following persons in any matter to be acted upon, other than elections to office: (1) each person who has been a director or officer of the issuer at any time since the beginning of the last fiscal year; (2) each nominee for election as a director; (3) each associate of the foregoing persons. Also give the name of any director who has informed management in writing that he intends to oppose any action to be taken and indicate the action he intends to oppose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 4 requires disclosure of interests and explicit identification of management opponents among directors with written notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule 14C Item 5 — Proposals by security holders and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If any security holder entitled to vote at the meeting has submitted to the issuer a proposal a reasonable time before the information statement is to be transmitted to security holders (other than elections to office), the statement shall make a statement to that effect, identify the proposal and indicate the disposition proposed to be made of the proposal by the management at the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: (1) a proposal submitted with respect to an annual meeting more than 60 days in advance of a day corresponding to the date of mailing will prima facie be deemed submitted a reasonable time before mailing; (2) if management intends to rule a proposal out of order, the Commission shall be advised at the time preliminary copies are filed, together with reasons why proposal is not a proper subject for action by security holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and revision marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any information statement filed is amended or revised, two of the copies of such amended or revised material filed shall be marked to indicate clearly and precisely the changes effected therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment alters text, the changes in text shall be indicated by underscoring or other appropriate manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission allowed where information unavailable with explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Information which is not known to the issuer and which it is not reasonably within the power of the issuer to ascertain or procure may be omitted, if a brief statement of the circumstances rendering such information unavailable is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Future-determined terms (e.g., terms of securities) may be stated in terms of present knowledge and intention; avoid omission of material items without explanatory note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies distribution within Commission and regional offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Four copies of the information statement will be kept in the Commission's principal office for the use of the staff and for public inspection; additional copies will be placed in the principal regional offices of the Commission and the regional office for the region in which the issuer has its principal office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distribution is intended to make information more readily available to interested persons in line with recommendations of the Special Study of Security Markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report transmission to Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report sent to security holders pursuant to these rules shall be mailed to the Commission, solely for its information, not later than the date on which such report is first sent or given to security holders or the date on which preliminary copies of the information statement are filed, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The annual report is not deemed "filed" with the Commission or subject to liabilities of section 18 except to the extent the issuer requests it to be treated as part of the information statement or incorporates it therein by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to certification of financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements included shall be certified by independent public or certified public accountants, unless (i) the corresponding statements included in the issuer's annual report filed or to be filed with the Commission for the same fiscal year are not required to be certified, or (ii) the Commission finds in a particular case that certification would be impracticable or would involve undue effort or expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these exceptions only where applicable and, if relied upon, be prepared to justify the impracticability or undue expense to the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical necessity statements for future-determined terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Any information required to be included as to terms of securities or other subject matters which from a standpoint of practical necessity must be determined in the future may be stated in terms of present knowledge and intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide present intent language and update/amend as appropriate when terms are fixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary exemption—combination drugs record-keeping (FDA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following drugs are exempt from the record-keeping requirements of section 511(d)(1) of the act on an interim basis until August 1, 1966: (a) drugs in unit-dosage form containing any quantity of a drug falling within the definition of a depressant or stimulant drug in section 201(v) of the act which may be lawfully sold over-the-counter without a prescription; (b) drugs containing amphetamines or barbiturates combined with other drugs; Provided, however, That this shall not apply to amphetamines or barbiturates combined with each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim exemption issued because files showed no evidence of significant abuse for such combinations; exemption effective on publication date and rescinds record-keeping requirements only until Aug 1, 1966.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of rewards — eligible offenses and maximums (Postal Service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the availability of funds, the Post Office Department will pay a reward for the arrest and conviction of any person for specified offenses with stated maximum amounts (examples include robbery: not to exceed $2,000 where custodian is wounded or life jeopardized; mailing of bombs or poison: not to exceed $2,000 for intent to kill or harm; lower maxima for other scenarios; theft, embezzlement, burglary, etc., with specified maxima).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed offense-by-offense caps and conditions are provided (see regulation): caps vary by offense and by aggravating circumstances; consult the specific enumerated provisions when assessing eligibility and maximum reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward amount determination factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of the reward to be paid will be based on the importance of services rendered, character of the offender, risks and hazards involved, time spent, and expenses incurred. Maximum rewards will be paid only when services were of the maximum value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations are discretionary and consider both qualitative and quantitative factors; do not assume maxima will automatically be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewards for accessories, receiving, and conspiracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Post Office Department also pays rewards for the arrest and conviction of any person as an accessory to any of the listed crimes; for receiving or having unlawful possession of any mail, money or property; and for conspiracy to commit any of the listed crimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accessory and related offenses are explicitly included; check the general provisions for applicability to reward claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims rejection and limiting awards (Postal Service)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will reject a claim where there has been collusion or improper methods used to effect an arrest or to secure a conviction. It has the right to allow only one reward where several persons were convicted of the same offense, or one person was convicted of several offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims are free of collusion or improper conduct; multiple convictions do not guarantee multiple awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim filing timeframe and procedure (Postal Service)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written claim must be submitted to the Postal Inspector in Charge of the division in which the crime was committed within 6 months from the date of conviction of an offender or the date of his death if killed in committing a crime or resisting arrest. Applications for filing of claims may be obtained from the Inspector in Charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing is mandatory; obtain and complete the official claim application from the relevant Postal Inspector's office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'custodian' (Postal Service)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'custodian' includes any person having lawful charge, control, or custody of any mail matter, or any money or other property of the United States under the control and jurisdiction of the Post Office Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition determines applicability of certain reward caps (e.g., robbery against a custodian).
